From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Position and Disclosure Letter

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package shifts almost all known risk to the Buyer. It caps and shortens general warranty protection, lumps title and tax into that regime, bars claims for matters the Buyer knows about, and resolves known issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the privacy incident) with vague or post-Completion mechanics. The known issues already total roughly AUD 4.1m or more, which is close to the proposed AUD 4.8m general cap. The Buyer should reject the general framework and insist on specific indemnities, price deductions, and conditions for the known matters.

This is a commercial and legal risk review based only on the documents provided. Points marked "verify" need confirmation from NSW and Commonwealth counsel before they go into a mark-up.

---

## 1. Warranty Architecture

| Seller position | Departure from Buyer interest | Pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) on general warranties (cl 12.1)** | About 20% of price is low for a 100% acquisition, and it is the Seller's total exposure for all general warranty claims. | Seek a cap of at least 30–50% of price. Fundamental warranties and tax should sit outside it. Known-issue exposure should be handled by specific indemnities, not by the warranty cap. |
| **De minimis AUD 25k per claim plus AUD 250k deductible basket (cl 12.2)** | The basket is a "deductible": the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k (about 1% of price). Combined with the per-claim de minimis, many small but related claims (e.g. supplier, employee and lease issues) would fall below threshold. | Seek a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar). Lower the de minimis or remove it, and aggregate related claims arising from the same facts. |
| **18-month claims period for general warranties (cl 12.3/13)** | Eighteen months may not cover a full audit or tax cycle, or the operation of the privacy and IP matters, which may surface later. | Seek 24–36 months for general warranties. Measure from Completion, not from notice. |
| **Limitation periods apply to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl 13)** | Makes the 18-month period the default for everything, including title and tax. | Reverse the default: fundamental and tax claims are excluded from general limitations unless expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental/title warranties subject to general caps and time limits** | Title and capacity are the core of what the Buyer is buying. A cap of 20% is inadequate, and an 18-month limit is too short. | Reject. Title, capacity and authority should be capped at the purchase price and survive for at least 6 years (verify against NSW limitation periods for contract claims; parties can agree longer periods within limits). |
| **Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"** | Unsupported. Tax and IP are high-risk for this target (the Ironquay issue shows this), and there is no tax indemnity in the Seller's package. | Require a standalone **pre-Completion tax indemnity** covering pre-Completion tax periods, with a survival period tied to the ATO amendment period (verify). Give IP warranties their own, longer survival period and cap. |

## 2. Limitations, Exclusive Remedy, Non-Reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

- **Departure:** These apply to "all Claims of any nature." That would capture fraud, title, and specific indemnities.
- **Pushback:** Carve out fraud, wilful misconduct, title and capacity, tax, and specific indemnities from all limitations and from the exclusive-remedy clause.
- **Non-reliance:** Ensure it does not exclude liability for fraud. Check how it interacts with misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (verify), since parties generally cannot contract out of fraud, and the ACL has its own protections that a contract clause may not override.

## 3. Disclosure Regime (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7)

- **Departure:** Disclosing the whole data room "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026," plus all public registers and statutory records, is a general disclosure that could cover almost anything in the documents. It effectively disclaims warranties on everything the Buyer could read.
- **Pushback:**
  - Limit disclosure to matters **specifically** disclosed against a specific warranty, in reasonable detail.
  - Reject general data room or public register disclosure. At most, documents the Seller has specifically listed and fairly disclosed.
  - Make clear that disclosure does not qualify fundamental or tax warranties, or specific indemnities.
  - Any updates or bring-downs to the disclosure letter should not cure breaches or prejudice the Buyer's termination or claim rights.
  - The 22 Sept 2026 date is now stale (today is 6 Nov 2026). Require a bring-down to Completion.

## 4. Buyer Knowledge (cl 8.3): Anti-Sandbagging

- **Departure:** The Buyer loses any claim for matters it or its advisers knew about, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Given the Buyer has now reviewed DD-002 to DD-012, this would bar claims on virtually all the known issues.
- **Pushback:** Delete. Insert an express **pro-sandbagging** clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice its rights to claim. The law on sandbagging is not settled in Australia, so the position must be stated expressly (verify).
- Address the known issues through **specific indemnities and price adjustments** instead, since warranty claims will be unavailable for them.

## 5. Specific Known Issues

### Bluefen (DD-002; AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30%)
- **Departure:** Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent. The disclosure confirms no final written consent and no evidence the conditions in cl 11.3 are satisfied. The Seller is therefore self-certifying satisfaction of a condition.
- **Pushback:**
  - Make written, unconditional Bluefen consent (including satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions) a **condition precedent** to Completion, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation.
  - Consent must be in agreed form, and the Buyer (not the Seller) decides whether conditions are satisfied.
  - If consent is not obtained, the Buyer should have a termination right and/or a price adjustment or escrow.

### Riverlark (DD-003; ~AUD 3.2m debt)
- **Departure:** Release "to follow Completion." The price is debt-free/cash-free, so the debt should be settled from the price at Completion. Leaving it unpaid means the Buyer's acquired company carries the debt and the Seller has the proceeds.
- **Pushback:** Require a **payoff letter and deed of discharge** of all security at Completion, with the amount deducted from the price as Indebtedness. Also address the change-control consent under cl 8.1.

### Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010; AUD 180k open)
- **Departure:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, and the Seller calls it adequate. The Project Materials transfer only on payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Pushback:**
  - The Seller pays the AUD 180k before Completion (or it is deducted as Indebtedness).
  - Require a **confirmatory assignment** of all Project Materials from Ironquay, with a warranty that title has passed.
  - Broaden the indemnity to all Ironquay claims (IP ownership, third-party claims, unpaid fees), uncapped or separately capped, and not limited to SOW3.

### Employee Bonuses (DD-005; AUD 420k)
- **Departure:** Excluded from the funds flow. The disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. The Seller says the matter is "for the Seller," but the funds flow does not reflect that.
- **Pushback:** Treat all Completion bonuses, plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, super, related taxes), as **Transaction Expenses or Indebtedness** deducted from price. Confirm amounts and conditions, and that the Seller bears any forfeiture or conditional-payment risk.

### Privacy/Export Incident (DD-006; ~1,240 records)
- **Departure:** Described as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The disclosure does not establish whether there was unauthorised access, the scope, or whether notification is required. The data includes names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- **Reasoning:** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), if the Company is an APP entity and there is a suspected eligible data breach, it must assess within 30 days and notify if required (verify current thresholds and penalty regime). The disclosure is dated 22 Sept, so that assessment window may already have run. This is time-sensitive.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require the Seller to commission a **forensic investigation** before Completion, with the Buyer's input.
  - Seek a **specific, uncapped indemnity** covering regulatory action, notification, remediation, third-party claims and costs.
  - Add a specific privacy-compliance warranty, not subject to the general disclosure regime.
  - Confirm whether a notification decision has been made.

### Office Lease (DD-007)
- **Departure:** Notification obligation identified, but no confirmation whether landlord consent is required for the share sale.
- **Pushback:** Obtain written landlord confirmation (or consent/estoppel) before Completion, or a specific indemnity for any landlord claim.

### Sandbar Supplier Renewals (DD-008, DD-011; AUD 330k aggregate)
- **Departure:** Called "ordinary-course," but the disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Three AUD 110k renewals sitting just above the de minimis threshold for each is worth noting.
- **Pushback:** Require confirmation of terms and termination rights. Any renewal commitments that bind the Company post-Completion for a cost not in the agreed working capital should be deducted from price or assumed by the Seller.

### Mossvale (DD-009)
- **Departure:** Restriction on assignment, but no confirmation whether a share sale triggers consent.
- **Pushback:** Obtain Mossvale's written confirmation that no consent is required (or obtain consent) as a pre-Completion deliverable, with a specific indemnity if it is required.

### Title (DD-012)
- **Departure:** The share register is the only source for title, and the disclosure notes the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Pushback:** Buyer to complete independent verification: current ASIC company extract, a PPSA search over the shares, confirmation of no options or other rights over shares, and a review of the full chain of title. Title warranty to be a fundamental warranty.

### Funds Flow
- **Departure:** Described as reflecting "agreed price mechanics," but it omits the bonuses and the Riverlark payoff.
- **Pushback:** Reconcile the funds flow against the debt-free/cash-free definitions. Confirm the price adjustment mechanism and that all Indebtedness and Transaction Expenses are deducted at Completion.

---

## 6. Recommendations Summary

**Reject outright:**
1. Anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3).
2. General data room and public register disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7).
3. Title and capacity capped and time-limited as general warranties.
4. Limitations applying to "all Claims" by default.
5. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language reaching fraud.

**Counter-propose:**
6. General cap of at least 30–50% of price, with fundamental and tax claims capped at purchase price.
7. Tipping basket, lower or no de minimis, aggregation of related claims.
8. 24–36 month general survival; 6-year-type survival for fundamental warranties (verify); tax tied to the ATO amendment period.
9. Pro-sandbagging clause.
10. Standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity and IP warranties with their own survival.
11. Specific, uncapped (or separately capped) indemnities for: Ironquay, the privacy incident, employee bonuses and on-costs, Sandbar renewals, Mossvale and the lease.

**Make conditions or completion deliverables:**
12. Written, unconditional Bluefen consent (with cl 11.3 satisfied) as a condition precedent, with a termination right if not obtained.
13. Riverlark payoff letter and discharge of security at Completion, deducted from price.
14. Ironquay AUD 180k paid pre-Completion, plus a confirmatory IP assignment.
15. Bonuses and on-costs deducted from price as Indebtedness or Transaction Expenses.
16. Forensic investigation of the privacy incident, plus a decision on notification.
17. Landlord and Mossvale confirmations.
18. Bring-down of disclosure to Completion, with updates not curing breaches.

**Buyer actions (not for the Seller):**
19. Complete independent title verification (ASIC extract, PPSA search, chain of title).
20. Obtain NSW and Commonwealth advice on the privacy notification timing, limitation periods, ACL interaction, and sandbagging.
21. Model the known-issue exposure (roughly AUD 4.1m before on-costs and Bluefen revenue risk) against the Seller's proposed cap to show the gap.

**Caveats:** This review relies only on the Seller's draft and disclosure letter. I have not seen the full SPA, the underlying data room documents, or the Buyer's existing due diligence reports. Statements about NSW limitation periods, Privacy Act timing and penalties, ACL interaction, and sandbagging should be verified by qualified counsel before use in negotiation.
